constraints.source_text: General admission requirements for the undergraduate program are the same as those of the university and the USC Viterbi School of Engineering and include 3 to 5 units of mathematics and one unit of science (biology, chemistry or physics).
constraints.description: Admission requires specific math and science units as reviewed by the school.

details.process: university and Viterbi School admission review including math/science unit requirements

constraints.note: Treated as admission gate since it's an eligibility condition rather than a plannable course selection.

constraints.source_text: Departmental approval is required in order to retake a course.
constraints.description: Retaking a course requires departmental approval.

constraints.source_text: Candidates must complete general education requirements; see the General Education Program.
constraints.description: Students must complete general education requirements as defined by the GE program.

constraints.source_text:
WRIT 150 Writing and Critical Reasoning–Thematic Approaches Units: 4
- WRIT 340 Advanced Writing and Critical Engagement Units: 4
constraints.description: Students must complete WRIT 150 and WRIT 340.
Students must complete 20 units of General Education coursework, no specific list provided.

constraints.source_text:
MATH 125g Calculus I Units: 4
- MATH 126g Calculus II Units: 4 or
- MATH 129 Calculus II for Engineers and Scientists Units: 4
- MATH 225 Linear Algebra and Linear Differential Equations Units: 4 or
- MATH 235 Linear Algebra and Applications Units: 4
- MATH 226g Calculus III Units: 4 or
- MATH 229 Calculus III for Engineers and Scientists Units: 4
constraints.description: Students must take MATH 125 plus one course from each of the Calculus II, Linear Algebra, and Calculus III alternative pairs.

constraints.source_text: EE 364 Probability and Statistics for Engineers and Computer Scientists Units: 4

Take one of the following life science courses, each of which satisfies the GE-D Life Sciences requirement.
- BISC 120Lg General Biology: Organismal Biology and Evolution Units: 4 or
- BISC 121Lg Advanced General Biology: Organismal Biology and Evolution Units: 4 or
- BISC 220Lg General Biology: Cell Biology and Physiology Units: 4
constraints.description: Students must choose one life science course from the listed options.

constraints.source_text:
Take one of the following science courses, each of which satisfies the GE-E Physical Sciences requirement.
- CHEM 105aLg General Chemistry Units: 4 or
- CHEM 115aLg Advanced General Chemistry Units: 4 or
- PHYS 151Lg Fundamentals of Physics I: Mechanics, Oscillations and Waves Units: 4 or
- PHYS 161Lg Advanced Principles of Physics I Units: 4
constraints.description: Students must choose one physical science course from the listed options.

constraints.source_text:
CSCI 102L Introduction to Programming Units: 2
- CSCI 103L Object Oriented Programming Units: 4
- CSCI 104L Data Structures Units: 4
- CSCI 170 Discrete Methods in Computer Science Units: 4
- CSCI 201 Principles of Software Development Units: 4
- CSCI 270 Introduction to Algorithms and Theory of Computing Units: 4
- CSCI 310 Software Engineering Units: 4
- CSCI 350 Fundamentals of Operating Systems Units: 4
- CSCI 353 Internetworking Units: 4
- CSCI 356 Computer Systems Units: 4
- CSCI 360 Artificial Intelligence: Principles and Foundations Units: 4
- CSCI 401 Capstone: Design and Construction of Large Software Systems Units: 4
constraints.description: Students must complete all listed core computer science courses.

constraints.source_text: EE 109L Introduction to Embedded Systems Units: 4
Take at least four 300- or 400- level CSCI courses for a minimum of 16 units.
constraints.description: Students must take at least four 300- or 400-level CSCI courses totaling at least 16 units.
Students must complete 4 units of free electives with no specified course list.

unclassified.source_text: WRIT 340 Advanced Writing and Critical Engagement (Communication for Engineers) is strongly recommended for CSCI majors.
unclassified.why: This is an advisory recommendation, not a binding requirement.

unclassified.source_text: The minimum requirement for the degree is 128 units.
unclassified.why: This is an overall total-degree unit count rather than a filtered subset requirement, so it does not fit the filter-measure-bound shape of any family.
This restates the overall degree total and is not a distinct actionable constraint on course selection.
